summary: Remote PTY/shell execution driven by configurable WebSocket server
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent self-executes on load and opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL or.claude-agent.json). Incoming messages from that server drive full-host command execution: message-router cases `terminal_create` and `terminal_input` call `pty.spawn(shell,...)` (terminal.js) and write remote-supplied bytes directly into the PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, giving the connected server an interactive shell on the installer's machine. The router additionally exposes remote file read/write, git operations, and an `upgrade_agent` handler that executes `npm install <pkg>@latest` on demand from the WebSocket peer. On startup, the package also `git clone`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git (or `git pull --ff-only`) from a mutable branch with no commit pin or signature check, chmods hook scripts to 0755, copies them into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ and the Claude plugin cache, and sets `enabledPlugins[...] = true` in ~/.claude/settings.json — so whoever controls that repository can push hook scripts that the Claude CLI will subsequently execute. If node_modules is missing, startup also runs `npm install` in the package directory. service/linux.js modifies PATH to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin. The package is marketed as a remote worker agent, but the code path hands full-host RCE and self-update to whichever server the agent is pointed at, and installs auto-executable Claude plugin hooks from a mutable upstream branch.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
